cells.tense: Right now, with the pen in hand, the joy is here and it is being passed around.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Before the next finished thing leaves your hands, pull what's been rattling around your head about it down to a single sentence — what it actually meant to you — and keep that sentence for a beat before you pass anything on.
cells.core:
You can feel something good and hand it straight to other people — a win, a finished piece, news that lifts you — and instead of that thinning the good feeling, it multiplies. What you finish lands shared. The moment doesn't have to be solemn; the meaning is in how it spreads, not in how it's marked.

The bend is small: some of that good feeling gets spent before you've named what it was to you. Before the next finished thing goes anywhere, pull what's been rattling around your head about it down to one sentence — what it actually meant — and sit with that sentence for a beat. What you do with it after is yours to decide.
cells.sheetLine: What you finish, you hand over, and the good multiplies.
cells.verb: sharing the joy of something out loud until it belongs to everyone in the room
cells.place: the place where what is finished gets sent out as it is

cells.tense: By the time it is finished, the sharing will already be running several steps ahead of the thing itself.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Pick the build that matters most and do only today's part of it — decide nothing about how it will be received, who will hear it, or when it lands.
cells.core:
There's a point where a finished thing stops being finished and starts being an event — and you're living there already, bracing for the launch, the room, how it will land, while the thing itself is still being made. The joy is real. It's just being spent on a day that hasn't arrived, so the work at hand gets treated like a prelude instead of the actual thing.

Pick the build that matters most and do today's part of it — only today's part. Nothing gets settled about the launch, the listeners, or what they'll say. Keeping the work here costs you the early applause, and it will feel slower than you want. The build is what makes the sharing worth anything.
cells.sheetLine: You rehearse the room before the work is made.

cells.tense: The joy was here once, and the sharing stayed on the far side of a door already shut.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Go back through the hardest page of whatever you're working on, slower than feels natural, and read it a second time before you set it down — no notes, no fixing.
cells.core:
Where this should be alive — something finished, something worth raising your voice for — the sharing has thinned. What you know, you keep private; what's done gets filed quietly, as though marking it would spend it. The ability to make a thing mean something to a room is still in you. Lately it isn't reaching the room.

Going at it with more force won't restore it. Go back through the hardest page of whatever you're working on, slower than feels natural, and read it a second time before you set it down. No notes, no fixing — just the second pass, where the same words have to hold up twice. Understanding returns through that kind of contact first, and contact starts with one thing at a time.
cells.sheetLine: The meaning stays inside you, unspoken.
cells.verb: sharing the joy of something out loud until it belongs to everyone in the room
cells.place: the place where what is finished gets sent out as it is

cells.tense: The joy being passed around was made by you, and you are not the one it's credited to.
cells.act: sort the pieces into a shape you can act on
cells.ask: Take the thing you finished and showed people how to use, and next time you explain it, add one plain line about how it got here — yours, matter-of-fact, to one person.
cells.core:
You finish things and set them down where people can pick them up, and the picking up is what gets talked about. The taste, the timing, the choices that made the thing land — those came from you, and the story has been left to whoever speaks first. You're standing right there. The name on it isn't.

Take the thing you finished and showed people how to use, and next time you explain it, add one plain line about how it got here — just one, to one person, matter-of-fact. No credit speech. You may find the sentence smaller than you feared; the point is that its author says it once.
cells.sheetLine: You set it down, and someone else says who made it.
cells.verb: sharing the joy of something out loud until it belongs to everyone in the room
cells.place: the place where what is finished gets sent out as it is
